title: Regular presentations and their intrinsic determinant under arbitrary base change
statement:
Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme (one admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]), let $f:X\to S$ be flat and locally of finite presentation [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and fix $d\geq0$. Assume $X$ is covered by presentations $U\xrightarrow{i}P\to S$, with $P$ open in $\mathbf A^n_S$ and $i$ a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] whose ideal $I$ is locally generated by a regular sequence $f_1,\ldots,f_c$ of length $c=n-d$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. For any morphism $S'\to S$, put $X'=X\times_SS'$, $U'=U\times_SS'$, $P'=P\times_SS'$, let $g:X'\to X$ and $g_U:U'\to U$ be the projections, and let $i':U'\hookrightarrow P'$ have ideal $I'$. Then, at every point of $U'$, the pulled-back equations form a regular sequence in the local ring of $P'$. On each pulled-back affine ambient chart their Koszul complex is exact in positive homological degrees, including away from $U'$, so they are Koszul-regular [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. With $C=I/I^2$, $C'=I'/I'^2$, $V=i^*\Omega^1_{P/S}$ and $V'=i'^*\Omega^1_{P'/S'}$, the natural maps $g_U^*C\xrightarrow{\sim}C'$ and $g_U^*V\xrightarrow{\sim}V'$ are isomorphisms of locally free modules of ranks $c,n$, sending the classes of the equations and coordinate differentials to their pulled-back classes and differentials. Use module pullback, differentials and exterior powers as in [def-pc-module-pullback, def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf, def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power]. Write $L=L_{X/S}$ and $L'=L_{X'/S'}$ for [lem-trf-lci-cotangent-presentation]. The square is Tor-independent, the natural comparison $Lg^*L\xrightarrow{\sim}L'$ is an isomorphism, and the induced map
$$g^*\det L\xrightarrow{\sim}\det(Lg^*L)\xrightarrow{\sim}\det L'$$
for [lem-trf-two-term-perfect-determinant] has local expression
$$g_U^*((\bigwedge^c C)^\vee\otimes\bigwedge^nV)\xrightarrow{\sim}(\bigwedge^c C')^\vee\otimes\bigwedge^nV'.$$
This expression is the map on tensors, exterior powers and duals induced by the two specified conormal and differential isomorphisms. It intertwines the presentation transitions obtained by taking determinants of the intrinsic conormal comparisons, and commutes with identity and composition of arbitrary base changes. No Noetherian assumption is imposed on $S'$.

proof.text: Work locally over $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$, on principal affine ambient charts $\operatorname{Spec}A\subset P$ where $A=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]_h$ and the ideal $J=(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$ is generated by the given regular sequence. These charts cover the presentation; further restrictions use the same argument. Put $B=A/J$. The affine flatness criterion applied to $f$ gives $R$-flatness of $B$. The polynomial projection is flat by [lem-nagata-polynomial-projection-flat]; the affine criterion and localization of flat modules give $R$-flatness of $A$. Also $A=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n,t]/(ht-1)$ is finitely presented over $R$. For an arbitrary affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}R'\subset S'$ above this base open, set $A'=A\otimes_RR'$ and $J'=(f_i\otimes1)$. The quotient-tensor isomorphism identifies $B'=B\otimes_RR'$ with $A'/J'$: its forward map is $(a\bmod J)\otimes r'\mapsto (a\otimes r')\bmod J'$ and its inverse sends $a\otimes r'$ to $(a\bmod J)\otimes r'$. This describes the pulled-back closed chart and equations.

Apply [lem-pur-relative-regular-equations-base-change] to $R\to A$, $R\to R'$ and $(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$. Its hypotheses are precisely regularity of this sequence, finite presentation and flatness of $A/R$, and flatness of $B/R$, verified in step 1. Thus at every prime $\mathfrak q'\supset J'$ the ordered images $f'_1/1,\ldots,f'_c/1$ form a regular sequence in $A'_{\mathfrak q'}$. These are exactly the ambient local rings at points of $U'$. The cited assertion requires no flatness or Noetherian hypothesis on $R'$.

The original equations are Koszul-regular by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-koszul-regular]. For the pulled-back equations, localize $K_{A'}(f')$ at an arbitrary prime $\mathfrak q'$. By [lem-sc-koszul-base-change-iso] this is the Koszul complex of their localized images. If $\mathfrak q'\supset J'$, step 2 and the same regular-to-Koszul lemma give zero positive homology. Otherwise some $f'_j$ is a unit in $A'_{\mathfrak q'}$. On the exterior presentation of the localized complex, define $h(w)=(f'_j)^{-1}e_j\wedge w$. The Koszul differential satisfies $d(e_j\wedge w)=f'_jw-e_j\wedge d(w)$, so $dh+hd=1$. Hence all localized homology vanishes there, including outside $U'$. Localization is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact], so it commutes with the kernels and image quotients defining homology. A nonzero homology class $z$ would remain nonzero at a maximal ideal containing its proper annihilator: $z/1=0$ would imply $sz=0$ for some $s$ outside that ideal, a contradiction. Consequently the positive homology vanishes on the whole affine ambient chart. The argument applies on every affine restriction where the equations are specified, and includes $c=0$.

By [lem-sc-koszul-conormal-basis] and step 3, the classes of $f_i$ and $f'_i$ are bases of $J/J^2$ over $B$ and $J'/J'^2$ over $B'$, respectively. The canonical conormal map is the map of [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-cotangent-flat-base-change-ring], after tensor reassociation: $B'\otimes_B(J/J^2)\to J'/J'^2$, $b'\otimes[f_i]\mapsto b'[f'_i]$. It sends a basis to a basis, with inverse $[f'_i]\mapsto1\otimes[f_i]$, and is therefore an isomorphism of rank $c$ modules. The affine tilde-pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-tilde-pullback-base-change] identifies it with $g_U^*C\to C'$. These formulas use only the ideal-induced map, so agree after restriction and glue to the specified conormal isomorphism, without requiring $A'$, $R'$ or $B'$ to be Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 062I (lemma-H1-regular-quasi-regular), first paragraph; morphisms.tex Tag 0473 (lemma-conormal-functorial-flat), affine map; schemes.tex affine tilde pullback.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-relative-differential-sheaf-base-change] to $P/S$ and restrict along $i'$. Pullback composition gives the specified isomorphism $g_U^*V\to V'$, whose formula is $1\otimes da\mapsto d(a\otimes1)$. The polynomial differential basis [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis-any-variables] and localization comparison [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization] identify $V$ with the free module on $dx_1,\ldots,dx_n$ on our chart. Their images give the corresponding basis of $V'$. Thus both differential modules have rank $n$, and the isomorphism carries coordinate differentials to their pulled-back differentials. The formulas agree on overlapping charts because they are induced by the universal derivations.

Flatness of $B/R$ also proves Tor-independence. Indeed specialize the base derived-tensor assertion of [lem-trf-base-flat-polynomial-tor-bound] to zero polynomial variables, $M=B$ and the $R$-module $R'$. It gives $B\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R'\simeq (B\otimes_RR')[0]=B'[0]$. Equivalently the flat complex $B[0]$ computes this derived tensor by ordinary tensor, with its canonical multiplication comparison. Apply [lem-trf-lci-cotangent-presentation] to this Tor-independent square. Its base-change assertion gives the intrinsic isomorphism $\beta:Lg^*L_{X/S}\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{X'/S'}$. Its conormal models apply on both sides, since step 3 proves Koszul-regularity even over the unrestricted new base. Its explicit compatibility with these models identifies $\beta$ locally with the chain map $[g_U^*C\to g_U^*V]\to[C'\to V']$ from steps 4--5: on the differential $[f_i]\mapsto df_i$ it commutes because $d(f_i\otimes1)$ is the image of $df_i$.

source.place: Tag 08QQ (lemma-flat-base-change-cotangent-complex), Tor-independent form; Tags 08SJ and 08SL for conormal models.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-two-term-perfect-determinant] to $\beta$ and its natural pullback comparison $\eta_g:g^*\det L\to\det(Lg^*L)$. Its two-term formula identifies $\det(\beta)\eta_g$ with the asserted local map $(\bigwedge^c C)^\vee\otimes\bigwedge^nV$ pulled back to the primed model. Explicitly, let $e=[f_1]\wedge\cdots\wedge[f_c]$ and $v=dx_1\wedge\cdots\wedge dx_n$. This map sends $1\otimes(e^\vee\otimes v)$ to $(e')^\vee\otimes v'$. The dual map here means the inverse transpose of the conormal exterior isomorphism, so it has this direction. This is exactly the tensor, exterior and dual map of the two basis isomorphisms; equality on this local generator proves equality of the line maps. Empty wedges equal $1$, so the formula also covers $c=0$ or $n=0$.

source.place: Tags 0FJX (lemma-determinant-two-term-complexes), 0FJY (remark-functorial-det), exterior formula and affine scalar extension.

proof.text: For completeness, write $\lambda_i:E_i\simeq L|_{U_i}$ for the intrinsic conormal comparisons. Compatibility in [lem-trf-lci-cotangent-presentation] says $\lambda'_i b_i=\beta\,Lg^*(\lambda_i)$, where $b_i$ is the chain isomorphism in step 6. Thus for $u_{ij}=\lambda_j^{-1}\lambda_i$, one has $b_j\,Lg^*(u_{ij})=(\lambda'_j)^{-1}\lambda'_i\,b_i$. Taking determinants and using naturality of $\eta_g$ from [lem-trf-two-term-perfect-determinant] gives $\delta_j g^*t_{ij}=t'_{ij}\delta_i$ for the local line maps $\delta_i$ of step 7 and $t_{ij}=\det u_{ij}$. This proves the required intertwining, even on non-affine overlaps by restriction. For $X''\xrightarrow{k}X'\xrightarrow{g}X$, cotangent comparison satisfies $\beta_{gk}=\beta_k\,Lk^*\beta_g$ under the specified pullback associator. Determinant functoriality and compatibility of $\eta$ with composition therefore give $\delta_{gk}=\delta_k k^*\delta_g$. Both comparisons are identities for the identity square. These equalities are intrinsic, hence agree with the displayed tensor/exterior/dual formulas on every presentation.

Live and side-live still have the item unsplit, and the item has no repair note: the resolved re-split note is on its parent lem-trf-flat-lci-canonical-adjunction, whose step 4 uses exactly this statement. Sources read: divisors 0FUD and more-algebra 0CEP. 0CEP's only hypothesis is that B/(f) is flat over A, for an arbitrary A->A'. 0FUD's 'every prime q'' is too broad, and the item and lem-pur-relative-regular-equations-base-change correctly restrict to primes containing J'. Perfect 0FJX/0FJY support the local determinant formula and the pullback comparison. No SGA is cited. Step 1: the affine flatness criterion on Spec B (an open of X lying over Spec R), polynomial flatness, localization of an R-flat A-module, finite presentation via ht-1, and the quotient-tensor identification. Step 2: the hypotheses of lem-pur-relative-regular-equations-base-change (A flat and finitely presented over R, (f) regular, A/(f) flat over R) all hold, and nothing is required of R'. Step 3: I recomputed dh+hd=1 for h(w)=f_j^{-1}e_j∧w from D(v∧x)=φ(v)x−v∧Dx; together with Koszul base change, exactness of localization and the annihilator argument, this proves def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence (3) on every chart, away from U' too. Step 4: Koszul-regular gives conormal bases; only the existence and formula of the 0473 map are used, not its flat-only injectivity, and it sends a basis to a basis. Step 5: arbitrary base change of differentials with the dx basis gives rank n. Step 6: base-flat Tor bound with n=0 and M=B gives the Tor-independence hypothesis of lem-trf-lci-cotangent-presentation; its conormal models apply because step 3 covers P'. Step 7: inverse transpose on the dual factor, and c=0 or n=0 are covered. Step 8: I recomputed b_j Lg^*u_ij = u'_ij b_i, then δ_j g^*t_ij = t'_ij δ_i and δ_gk = δ_k k^*δ_g. Edge cases: c=0, R'=0, Z[x] with f=x over F_2 (allowed), f=2 (excluded since B is not flat), and charts missing U (only charts meeting U need the regular-sequence hypothesis).
